item.title: A bit confused, but heck, I'm new, so ignore me if I'm wrong.
item.content:encoded: So, gotta be honest, this was a cool little SCP. Really liked the concept and everything, so good on you man, good on you! But I'm a little confused as to why this is rated as an Euclid class SCP. Maybe I'm wrong on this, but I thought that Euclid's are supposed to be, in some way shape or form, dangerous. And, no offense, but come on. It's talking bread. I just don't see how bread, or the recipe it's specifically derived from, could be dangerous. The only thing I could think of is the emotional distress you'd likely feel from eating it or if you choked on it. Again, I could be wrong, but I'd consider just labeling it as "Safe".

I freely confess to loving this concept, mostly because it is stupid and stupidly entertaining to picture. My sister made this creepy little craft ages ago for some kindergarten project, that inexplicably required her to glue little googley eyes and a felt smile to a stale piece of toast. But just baaaarely decided to upvote, because your scientific tone really needs some work.

+and here is what I mean by that...
– hide block

when a loaf of bread is created by a subject who is only following directions from SCP-613 or memory of it without consulting any other sources

this is clumsily phrased, and sucks out the momentum leading to your "it comes to liiiiiiife" punchline

SCP-613-1 are loaves of bread created while following the directions on SCP-613.

you just said that— combine or cut

will have average mental states and intelligence, however, instances that rise at non-room temperatures will have chances of developing mental disorders and/or increasingly non-average IQ

hold up, "average"? Compared to WHAT, exactly? Other loaves of bread? Chimps? Sentient grapes? Human beings? That's an important clarification.

There are currently no identified factors that appear to control whether the IQ will increase or decrease.

this is either mis-phrased or contradicts what you just said

disparate identities distinct from the parent instance of SCP-613-1. Instances of SCP-613 produced in this manner have been observed to engage in erratic movements and vocalizations indicative of physical pain

this is especially subjective, but I think you should either elaborate a bit on this effect or trim it down; you mention "personalities" a bit without really explaining what you mean

sporadically appearing around the world

this isn't very scientifically phrased

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This just…doesn't work for me. I mean, the core concept of baking sentient loaves of bread is workable, I think, but you didn't really *do* anything with it. Something like this is begging for a well-written interview log, and there just isn't one.

On top of that, the tone is kind of erratic and the recovery log doesn't add much. It felt a bit cop-out-y how you had literally one line saying "oh and no one knows or will tell us where they learned the recipe". Seriously? With the questioning methods I have to assume the Foundation possesses, I would think we would know for certain whether they knew where they got them or not.

All in all, there is no one specific thing about it I loathe, and it is a solid effort, but it just isn't fleshed out enough for my tastes.

Also, come on, throw in a picture. I know they aren't mandatory, but photos do a lot to make an SCP more enjoyable to read, and I don't think it's terribly difficult to find a photo of a loaf of bread.
